note: Source-of-truth manifest for refresh.js. For every dataset, this records the live doc URL (what the UI cites) and the markdown file backing it (what refresh.js parses). The markdown paths come from the 'Edit this page' link on each rendered page. When Elastic moves or renames a page, THIS is the only file that needs updating.

verifiedLegend.scrape-2026-09-09: mdPath was read directly off the page's 'Edit this page' link during the original scrape. High confidence.
verifiedLegend.inferred-from-sibling: mdPath follows the same directory convention as a sibling page whose path WAS observed. Likely correct; refresh.js reports a 404 clearly if not.
verifiedLegend.unverified-guess: The URL slug and the repo directory name may differ (e.g. /edot-sdks/node vs docs/reference/edot-sdks/nodejs/). refresh.js resolves these by listing the repo tree, and reports what it found.
verifiedLegend.NOT-IN-elastic/opentelemetry: Observed fact, not a guess: this page has no markdown in elastic/opentelemetry. mdPath is null so refresh.js skips it rather than reporting a misleading 404. The page is still cross-checkable from its rendered HTML once a repo is identified.
verifiedLegend.resolved-from-tree: mdPath was taken from an actual repo tree listing via --resolve-paths. Highest confidence.
